new_result.statement: For disjoint product banks Z,X, scalar projection W=u^T Z with density cap M, orthonormal leaf projections L=q^T X,V=p^T X with max_i(q_i^2+p_i^2)<=1/2, arbitrary internal hub-bank phase F(Z), arbitrary diagonal leaf quadratic and affine terms, and carrier B=[[A,nu,0],[nu,alpha,beta],[0,beta,lambda]] with lambda!=0 and lambda*det(B)<0, the quadratic form has |phi(t)|<=4*pi^(3/2)*M*|det B|^(-1/2)*|t|^(-3/2) and ||p||_infinity<=3*2^(4/3)*M^(2/3)*|det B|^(-1/3); its density is continuous and C0.
new_result.mechanism: Complete the LV square; make a real hub shear solving A c^2-2 nu c+(alpha-beta^2/lambda)=0; retain only the pointwise projection-density cap on the resulting dependent hub amplitude; the leaf column shear preserves normalized row leverages exactly; finish with original-coordinate mixed Fresnel and geometric Brascamp-Lieb.
new_result.projection_theorem_use: For normalized W=u^T Z, the actual bounded-density projection theorem gives M<=sqrt(2), hence ||p||_infinity<=3*2^(5/3)|det B|^(-1/3). The projection cap is used only before nonlinear integration, not as indefinite coarea.

strict_target_example.form: Q_*=H^2+4HL+L^2+2LV+2V^2 with diffuse orthonormal Walsh L,V

partner_applied.actual_inequality: For Q_0=H^2+4HL+2V^2 on a diffuse Walsh leaf plane, the partner diffuse branch gives ||p_Q0||_infinity<=3*2^(1/3)=3.77976314968..., and the carrier spectrum {2,(1+sqrt(17))/2,(1-sqrt(17))/2} lies in the owner target.

remaining_implication.statement: Decompose same-bank T=T_parallel+eps P with P perpendicular to span{L,V}. The new theorem removes T_parallel exactly in the hyperbolic Schur-sign diffuse branch. Moderate nonzero eps is paid only with a deteriorating |eps|^(-1/3) cost. Prove a uniform bridge eps->0 while retaining rough cap-one laws and arbitrary additional non-diagonal same-bank residual curvature, or force a source-separated relay.

next_step: Attack the transverse eps->0 bridge by keeping the LP phase inside a TT*/Hilbert or fractional grouped-crossing estimate instead of replacing the adapted hub by a conditional-density cap.
